newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Jews to seek Nazi war criminal Brunner.
newsitem.headline: Greek Jews to seek Nazi war criminal Brunner.

text.p: Greek Jews said on Wednesday they would seek the extradition from Syria of Nazi war criminal Alois Brunner, blamed for the deaths of 120,000 European Jews.
"We will make an official request to the Greek Justice ministry this week," Nissim Mais, president of the central board of the Jewish Community of Greece, told Reuters.
"This man was active in Salonika, where more than 50,000 Greek Jews were murdered."
Brunner, the Austrian-born SS commander and right-hand man of Adolph Eichmann, is believed to be in Syria, a country which is on good terms with Greece, he said.
"Brunner is in Syria but we cannot ask for his extradition because Greece waived its rights on the prosecution of World War Two criminals," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.
He said that Greece transferred its extradition rights in 1959 to the then West Germany.
"Our legal experts are looking into whether this can be overcome and go directly to Syria," Mais said. "If not, then we want Greece to request Germany to act on its behalf."
Mais said the initiative was prompted by news reports that Brunner was alive and well and has been living in Damascus for the past 38 years. He would now be 84 years old.
"We know that he is so old that he might drop dead during his arrest. But it's not the man we care about, but his actions and his ideas," he said.

Thought to be the last of the senior Nazi criminals still alive, Brunner operated in the northern Greek city of Salonika, where almost the entire community of 60,000 Jews was sent to the gas chambers in 1943.

"We know that he was methodical in his purpose, which was to eradicate Jews from the face of the earth. His victims were people of all ages and both sexes," said Mais, whose community now has 5,000 members nationwide.

Salonika's Jewish history dates back to the second century BC and St Paul preached at its synagogue. The city known at the turn of the century as the second Jerusalem now has a dwindling community of 1,000 Jews.
A month after Brunner's arrival, cattle trains began taking Jews from Salonika to Auschwitz, deporting almost the entire Jewish population in a few months.

Brunner also served as commandant of the Drancy transit concentration camp on the outskirts of Paris. Altogether he is blamed for the deaths of 120,000 Jews from Greece, the former Czechoslovakia, France and Austria.
